description: Category boards. Each board has categories, each with clues at rising point values. The player picks a cell, reads the clue, and types the answer (the 'in the form of a question' phrasing is accepted but not required). Every clue carries an authoritative citation.

clues.clue: The gateway to the other sacraments, it frees from original sin and makes one a member of the Church.
clues.explanation: Baptism regenerates the person as a child of God and cannot be repeated.

clues.clue: This sacrament seals the baptized with the Gift of the Holy Spirit and completes baptismal grace.
clues.explanation: Confirmation more perfectly binds the Christian to the Church and strengthens them for witness.

clues.clue: Also called Penance and Confession, this sacrament restores a person to grace after grave sin.
clues.explanation: Through the priest's absolution God grants pardon and peace to the contrite sinner.

clues.clue: God set a rainbow in the sky as the sign of His covenant with this man after the flood.
clues.explanation: The covenant with Noah remains in force as long as the world lasts, embracing all living creatures.

clues.clue: At this mountain Moses received the Law, and the covenant was sealed with the blood of sacrifice.
clues.explanation: The Sinai covenant made Israel a priestly people belonging to God.

clues.clue: God promised this king that his throne and his house would be established forever, a promise fulfilled in Christ.
clues.explanation: The everlasting kingdom promised to David is realized in the reign of his descendant, the Messiah.

clues.clue: The Creed professed at Sunday Mass takes its name from councils held in 325 and 381.
clues.explanation: It draws on the great councils of Nicaea and Constantinople and is common to East and West.

clues.clue: Added at Nicaea, this term means 'of the same substance' and affirms that the Son is fully God.
clues.explanation: Against Arius, Nicaea confessed the Son as consubstantial with the Father.

clues.clue: The Creed names these four marks of the Church.
acceptedAnswers: What are one, holy, catholic, and apostolic
clues.explanation: These four inseparable marks identify the Church Christ founded.

clues.clue: The Lord taught this prayer of seven petitions when the disciples asked Him how to pray.
clues.explanation: The Catechism calls the Lord's Prayer the summary of the whole Gospel.

clues.clue: One of the three major expressions of prayer, it rests wordlessly in God's presence, a 'gaze of faith.'
clues.explanation: Contemplative prayer is a silent love that keeps its eyes fixed on Jesus.

clues.clue: This Old Testament book of 150 prayers is prayed daily by the Church in the Liturgy of the Hours.
clues.explanation: The Psalms are the masterwork of prayer in the Old Testament and remain the Church's own.

clues.clue: This bishop of Hippo wrote the Confessions and The City of God.
clues.explanation: Augustine is among the most influential of the Western Fathers and Doctors of the Church.

clues.clue: The Angelic Doctor, this Dominican wrote the Summa Theologiae and the Corpus Christi hymns.
clues.explanation: The Catechism quotes Aquinas's Eucharistic hymn Adoro te devote.

clues.clue: This deacon and later bishop of Alexandria stood almost alone against Arianism and was exiled five times.
clues.explanation: Athanasius defended the Nicene confession of Christ's full divinity through decades of exile.

clues.clue: The Mass has two principal parts: the Liturgy of the Word and this.
acceptedAnswers: What is the Liturgy of the Eucharist
clues.explanation: Word and Eucharist together form one single act of worship.

clues.clue: The change of the whole substance of bread and wine into Christ's Body and Blood is called this.
clues.explanation: The appearances of bread and wine remain, but the reality is now Christ Himself.

clues.clue: The Mass is not a new sacrifice but the making-present of this one event.
acceptedAnswers: What is the sacrifice of the Cross
clues.explanation: The Eucharist re-presents the one sacrifice of Calvary and applies its fruit.

clues.clue: This dogma holds that Mary, from the first instant of her conception, was preserved free from original sin.
clues.explanation: Mary was preserved immaculate by a singular grace, in view of the merits of Christ.

clues.clue: At the end of her earthly life, Mary was taken body and soul into heavenly glory; this is called her ___.
clues.explanation: The Assumption is a singular sharing in her Son's Resurrection and anticipates the glory of all the redeemed.

clues.clue: The Council of Ephesus in 431 defended this title of Mary, meaning 'God-bearer.'
clues.explanation: Because her Son is one divine person, Mary is truly Mother of God.

clues.clue: The four last things are death, judgment, heaven, and this.
clues.explanation: Hell is the state of definitive self-exclusion from communion with God.

clues.clue: This is the final purification of those who die in God's grace but are still imperfectly purified.
clues.explanation: The purification of purgatory is entirely different from the punishment of the damned.

clues.clue: At the end of time Christ returns in glory and all the dead rise for this event.
clues.explanation: The Last Judgment reveals the ultimate meaning of the whole work of creation and salvation.
